newsitem.title: UK: IPE GAS OIL CLOSES 75 CTS DOWN, BRENT AT $18.81.
newsitem.headline: IPE GAS OIL CLOSES 75 CTS DOWN, BRENT AT $18.81.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures closed 75 cents easier in listless trade and in a narrow range on Wednesday, preventing from dipping further by U.S. gasoline strength.
Front month September settled at $170.00 a tonne, 75 cents down from the high and just 50 cents off the low. October settled at $172.00.
"It's been less than exciting," said one broker. "There was a complete lack of trade interest and it's just been locals pushing and pulling it about."
"The only saviour was gasoline in the States."

U.S. gasoline was fired up by rumours of a snag of Exxon's Baytown catalytic cracker in Houston, Texas and news that Exxon was in the market buying product. An Exxon source said Baytown was running its cracker after a leak but was considering a short shutdown for repairs.
Support for October gas oil was put at $178.50/$179 with good support at $171.

IPE Brent crude futures continued to retrace morning lossses. September IPE Brent was trading four cents weaker at $18.81 a barrel at 1649 GMT, 11 cents firmer than its midday level and one cent off its high.
Dealers said any break above $20.00 a barrel on front month WTI could trigger gains on Brent but said the New York contract looked unlikely to make any sizeable further gains.
Daily high/low support was at intact at $18.55 and key trendline support at $18.40 below this. October Brent was facing resistance at $18.95 a barrel.
Values shrugged off further headlines about Iraq. U.N. officials said overseers had approved 12 Iraqi contracts for the second round of the "oil for food" deal to August 12.
Gasoline was trading 1.09 cent firmer at 64.80 cents a gallon. Heating was 0.15 cent firmer at 55.25 cents.
